The new "Change status:" authoritative signal is a good architectural improvement. The logging of git diff stats at success will help debug future issues.; The pattern inconsistency between review_autofix.yml and review_apply_fixes.sh should be resolved. The script-level detection at review_apply_fixes.sh needs the "no changes" patterns restored, while the workflow-level detection at lines 2037 and 2059 should use the comprehensive informational-bullet pattern for consistency with the main detection path.

LOW CONFIDENCE (flagged by 1 reviewer only):
  [3] File: scripts/review_apply_fixes.sh (line ~640)
      Problem: The grep pattern for filtering non-substantive change claims was updated to include new informational bullets (e.g., `Validation limitation`, `Ran [^:]*(validation|check|test)`) but it incorrectly removed the patterns for "no changes" declarations (`No .* modified`, `No changes`).; When the editor reports no changes using bullet points like "- No files modified" or "- No changes" in the "Changes made:" section (which is common and correct behavior), these lines will now pass through the filter. This results in `_claimed_changes` being non-empty. Since the editor did not actually write any files, `_git_has_diff` will be `false`, triggering the `EDITOR_CHANGES_LOST` error and blocking auto-merge with a false-positive alert.
      Confidence: avg 5.0
      Flagged by: google_gemini-3-flash-preview

  [4] File: scripts/review_apply_fixes.sh
      Problem: The substantive detection regex was expanded to include new informational bullet patterns (Validation limitation, Ran validation/check/test, Assumptions made/applied, Missing-context) but removed the prior "no changes" exclusion patterns ("No .* modified", "No .* changed", "No .* touched", "No changes").; While the comprehensive pattern now correctly filters validation/assumption bullets per the PR intent, the removal of "no changes" patterns means editor outputs like "- No files modified" or "- No changes" will pass through the filter. In review_apply_fixes.sh (unlike review_autofix.yml), there is no separate "no changes" handling logic - the filter is the only guard. When an editor reports "- No files modified", this will be treated as substantive claimed changes and trigger the EDITOR_CHANGES_LOST warning if git shows no diff.
      Confidence: avg 4.0
      Flagged by: moonshotai_kimi-k2_5

  [5] File: .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml (line ~2037)
      Problem: The first `grep` in the warning path (triggered when `change_status` is "not-edited" but the section has content) only filters `Validation executed`. It has not been updated with the comprehensive list of informational patterns added elsewhere in this PR (e.g., `Validation limitation`, `Ran ...`, `Assumptions ...`).; If an editor emits one of the new informational bullets (like "- Assumptions applied") and sets `change_status: not-edited`, this line will pass the first filter. While the subsequent keyword-based `grep` (looking for "modif", "update", etc.) might still avoid a match, the inconsistency represents a logic gap that can lead to false "contradiction" warnings if an informational bullet happens to contain one of the edit-related keywords.
      Confidence: avg 4.0
      Flagged by: google_gemini-3-flash-preview

      Problem: Similar to line 2037, this `grep` (used when the authoritative `Change status:` field is missing or malformed) has not been updated to include the new informational bullets. It only filters `Validation executed`.; If the authoritative status is missing and the editor provides informational bullets, these lines will be included in the `substantive` variable. This can interfere with the "first line check" logic or contradiction detection later in that block, as the script will treat informational bullets as potentially substantive claims of change.
      Confidence: avg 4.0

      Problem: The logic to split the tab-separated `_pr_gate` variable (`state` and `merged`) relies on shell parameter expansion that might be brittle depending on the environment or the presence of unexpected tabs.; If `_pr_gate` contains unexpected formatting or if the tab character `$'\t'` is not handled correctly by the specific version of Bash used in the runner, `pr_merged` might end up containing the full string (e.g., `open	false`). If the string comparison `[ "${pr_merged}" = "${_pr_gate}" ]` fails to catch this, the workflow will attempt to `tr` the full string, resulting in an invalid `pr_merged` value that might break the subsequent numeric/state checks.; HARDENING_SUGGESTIONS:
